_why: cs #383·AI. After the C0108 re-cut seed 108 teaches 'expect', and 'hope' is next taught at S0151. (1) Seed 149's canonical target 'This isn't very difficult, so I hope you'll finish soon.' needs 'hope': the seed is not touched; the shortest LEGO 'hope' (known 'බලාපොරොත්තු වෙනවා', the seed's own known word; Malalasekera English-Sinhalese Dictionary, s.v. hope / expect: බලාපොරොත්තු වෙනවා covers both, so the English target is what the learner says) is inserted as S0149L02 with 10 rows (4 BUILD, 6 USE) on the shape of the existing S0149L01 rows. The two S0149L01 BUILD rows that said 'I hope' come before that LEGO, so they are re-said without it ('I believe' as in S0149L01U07; 'so you'll finish soon'), and their old sentences move into the new basket. (2) Seventeen rows in seeds 109-126 said 'hope'. Fourteen are deleted (thin basket over a bad row, Kai 19 Nov): most were already broken English ('I hope for our brain', 'I hope in the pub about that') and their known side says ආශා (desire), not the taught verb; re-saying them with 'expect' cannot pass the builder (each seed is validated without the 108 overlay; 'expect' is next taught at S0404). The three BUILD rows among them (S0111L01B02, S0121L01B03, S0126L01B03) are re-said with taught words instead, because those baskets are at their BUILD minimum: 'about our brain', 'about your car', 'I know the shape of that'. Baskets keep 9-11 rows each. (3) ZUT: S0291L01B01 gave the bare 'බලාපොරොත්තු වෙනවා' (now the hope LEGO's known) for 'I hope I'll be able to'; its known is re-said on its own basket's pattern ('මම ... ලැබෙයි කියලා බලාපොරොත්තු වෙනවා', as S0291L01U01-U11 and S0668L01B01) so one prompt keeps one answer.
